title: SLO restitution orchestrator and burn-rate reconciler
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Problem: We lack a consistent, automated way to translate SLI shortfalls into tracked initiatives and to reconcile initiative burn against error budgets across product, infra, and on-call owners. This creates ad-hoc responses, duplicated remediation efforts, and opaque prioritization when an SLO is breached.

Goal: Build an SLO restitution orchestrator that automates creation and lifecycle tracking of remediation initiatives when defined SLI windows cross thresholds (grace/violation). The orchestrator will: 1) create a standardized initiative artifact in Linear or populate an initiative template; 2) assign owners based on a configurable stewardship matrix; 3) calculate a normalized burn-rate score; 4) attach relevant telemetry snapshots and incident links; 5) feed to the Initiative Hub dashboard and alerting rules so leadership sees rollups and runway impact.

Why now: Multiple teams (Serving Runtime, Console, Dedicated) have reported opaque error-budget consumption patterns during spikes. This work reduces mean-time-to-remediate (MTTR) for reliability regressions, improves prioritization of engineering effort, and makes rollback/mitigation decisions faster during critical windows.
acceptance_criteria: When an SLI window exceeds the configured warning threshold, the system creates a draft initiative with standardized title, description template, and attached telemetry snapshot.
Initiative creation includes suggested owner(s) from stewardship matrix and a recommended remediation priority based on normalized burn-rate (score > 1.0 => priority P0/P1 mapping).
Initiative dashboard shows live rollup of active SLO restitution initiatives with burn-rate, affected customers, and expected runway impact.
Teams can opt to acknowledge/claim an initiative via the dashboard or Linear workflow and update status that flows back into the SLO ledger within 1 hour.
Automated weekly reconciliation job summarizes resolved initiatives and adjusts projected error-budget runway metrics in Initiative Hub reports.
success_metrics: Reduce time from SLO breach detection to owner acknowledgment to < 60 minutes for 80% of events within 90 days of launch.
Reduce duplicate remediation initiatives for the same SLO incident to < 10% (de-duplication by telemetry fingerprint).
Increase visibility: 100% of SLO breaches generate an initiative or a documented exemption in the first 30 days.
Demonstrate a 20% reduction in manual triage hours spent across on-call and PMs for SLO-related work in quarter following rollout.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Design, 2 weeks): Define stewardship matrix, initiative template fields, burn-rate formula and thresholds. Deliver spec in Confluence: /confluence/rh/slo-restitution/spec.

Phase 2 (Prototype, 3 sprints): Build a lightweight service that listens to SLO alerts, queries telemetry snapshots, and creates draft Linear initiatives via API. Include opt-in toggle per product. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/slo-orch/pull/12.
Phase 3 (Integration, 2 sprints): Wire to Initiative Hub dashboard, add acknowledgment workflow and claim button; implement de-duplication by trace fingerprint and similar hash.
Phase 4 (Reconciliation & Reporting, 2 sprints): Weekly reconciliation job, export to weekly reliability digest, and adjust Initiative Hub runway projections.
Phase 5 (Rollout & Training): Pilot with Serving Runtime team for 4 weeks, gather feedback, then enable for Console + Dedicated in staggered waves.
rollout_plan: Pilot: Enable for serving/runtime SLOs only. Notify pilot teams and run daily sync for 2 weeks.
Wave 1: Enable for Console SLOs after pilot signoff; provide 1-hour office hours for first week.
Wave 2: Enable for Dedicated and Private SLOs with additional RBAC checks and customer-impact tagging.
Full: Enable default automation for all SLOs, with an 'opt-out' toggle for team leads.
